basis: jinshu:053:s0034 explicitly names 賈后母郭槐 and her proposed marriage between the crown prince and 韓壽女. zizhitongjian:083:s0126 names 廣城君郭槐, and s0128 repeats the same Han Shou daughter marriage proposal, refused by 賈午 and the empress in s0129. The shared full Chinese name, maternal position and specific unsuccessful marriage plan establish the same woman, not a surname-only match.

jinshu:031:s0574 calls the woman 后母廣城君 and describes her urging kindness toward 愍懷; s0575 has her rebuke 賈謐. These distinctive acts match zizhitongjian:083:s0126–s0127. The complete s0571–s0583 and Tongjian s0126–s0135 narratives retain the same empress/heir/Jia Mi family frame.

jinshu:031:s0576 explicitly changes 廣城君 to 宜城: 及廣城君病篤，占術謂不宜封廣城，乃改封宜城. The same dying woman in s0578–s0579 holds the empress’s hand, urges care for the prince, and warns against 趙粲及午, matching zizhitongjian:083:s0131–s0134. Thus Guangcheng and Yicheng are successive titles of this woman.

Independent primary witness jinshu:040:s0147 explicitly identifies 充婦廣城君郭槐. In the same Jia Chong family account, s0172 says 賈后擅權…母郭為宜城君, and s0173 records 郭氏’s death. Together with Jinshu053s0034, this directly connects Guo Huai, Empress Jia’s mother, to the Yicheng title.

jinshu:053:s0074–s0106 is Sima Yu’s letter, not narrator-issued genealogy. Its s0077 自宜城君亡 refers retrospectively to the death of this Lady of Yicheng, consistent with Jinshu031’s narrated death and kindness toward Yu. Current p056 contains only the title/death/care context and no claim that she was Lady Xie’s mother; merge it with the other three current records without restoring the removed false parentage.
